record.paper_title: Dima Khavinson’s 60th: a summary of open problems in analysis and mathematical physics
record.original_question: The case α = 2 of the nonlinear Loewner-type growth equation has been studied extensively. What special behavior occurs at α = 1, where the boundary’s normal velocity is heuristically constant and the evolution is compared with the α = 1 Hastings-Levitov/Eden-type regime?

evidence.quote: The special value α = 2 has been studied extensively. What about the case α = 1?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following family of nonlinear Loewner-type planar growth processes. Let $K_0 = \overline{\mathbb{D}}^c \cup \{\infty\}$ be the exterior of the closed unit disk, and consider a growing family of compact hulls $K_t \supset K_0$, $t \ge 0$, in the Riemann sphere whose complements are simply connected. For each $t$, let $g_t : \mathbb{C} \setminus K_t \to \{|z|>1\}$ be the unique conformal map fixing $\infty$ with $g_t'(\infty)>0$. Given a parameter $\alpha > 0$ and a probability measure $\mu_t$ on the unit circle, the family $(g_t)$ is required to satisfy the weighted Loewner-Kufarev equation
$$\partial_t g_t(z) = g_t(z) \int_{|\zeta|=1} \frac{g_t(z)+\zeta}{g_t(z)-\zeta} \, |g_t'(z)|^{-\alpha}\bigg|_{\text{boundary push-forward}} \, d\mu_t(\zeta),$$
so that, heuristically, the inward normal velocity of the boundary $\partial K_t$ at a point $w \in \partial K_t$ is proportional to $|g_t'(w)|^{\alpha-1}$ times a local driving density. The case $\alpha = 2$ corresponds to Hele–Shaw / Laplacian growth and has been studied extensively (Carleson–Makarov and others), where one obtains existence, scaling limits, and information on the limit shapes.

Investigate the case $\alpha = 1$, in which the normal velocity of the boundary is (formally) a constant independent of conformal distortion, so that the evolution is heuristically an Eden-type isotropic growth and is conjecturally related to the $\alpha = 1$ Hastings–Levitov regime $\mathrm{HL}(1)$. Specifically: establish existence and uniqueness of solutions $K_t$ for natural classes of driving measures $\mu_t$; describe the scaling limit and the regularity (e.g. smoothness or roughness) of $\partial K_t$; and determine whether the limit shapes coincide with, or qualitatively differ from, those produced by random $\mathrm{HL}(1)$ / Eden aggregation in an appropriate scaling limit.
artifact.status_search_result: The α = 1 case of nonlinear Loewner-driven planar aggregation (and the related Hastings–Levitov HL(1) model) is widely identified as a critical and subtle regime. While the α = 2 (Hele–Shaw/Laplacian) case is well developed via Carleson–Makarov and successors, no complete description of existence, scaling limits, and limit shapes for the α = 1 deterministic Loewner growth or rigorous matching with HL(1) appears in the literature as of 2026; partial results exist for anisotropic/regularized Hastings–Levitov families and related stationary HL(0) models, but the α = 1 case remains open.

status_evidence.title: Aggregation in the Plane and Loewner's Equation
status_evidence.snippet: Carleson–Makarov foundational work on the α=2 Laplacian growth model via the Loewner equation.
status_evidence.claim: The α=2 case is the well-studied benchmark; other α remain less understood.

status_evidence.title: Scaling limits of anisotropic Hastings-Levitov clusters
status_evidence.snippet: Hastings and Levitov predicted a change in behaviour for HL(α) when α=1.
status_evidence.claim: α=1 is identified as a critical transition for the HL family, with no full rigorous theory.

status_evidence.title: Dima Khavinson's 60th: a summary of open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open problems in analysis and mathematical physics including questions about α=1 in Loewner-type growth.
status_evidence.claim: Problem listed as open in 2018 summary.
